limitations: Source-derived candidate; no local efficacy validation.
Original typed source inventory is not normalized; retain source identities and limits in the procedure/readsets.

applicability.scope: Run a bounded, accuracy-gated tuning campaign for a single Ascend operator already identified as the bottleneck, escalating from code-level to scheduling and instruction-level changes.
applicability.prerequisites: A measured operator baseline, an explicit numeric target and a logged on-device accuracy pass before tuning; performance comparisons use real hardware.
applicability.input_contract: Operator implementation, fixed shape/dtype/card and warmup policy, accuracy result, per-core work/wait measurements and round logs.
applicability.produced_artifact: A bounded campaign record of each change, accuracy and measured timing delta, kept/reverted rounds, current stage and documented stop condition.
applicability.refusal_point: Do not start without the baseline and accuracy gate; revert accuracy failures, and stop/escalate repeated failures, timeouts, exhausted stages or the campaign budget.
applicability.failure_modes: Scheduler-idle and predecessor-wait bottlenecks need different fixes; output inplace-reshape can corrupt slice writes, and a changed analyzer log format can produce a misleading zero-core report.

recommendations: Change one parameter and recheck accuracy each round; keep the failure record when reverting and compare the final configuration against the same baseline workload and warmup policy.
Route scheduler bubbles separately from predecessor dependencies and enter instruction-level tuning only after isolating a specific long task.
Verify the analyzer parsed real cores before trusting its diagnosis, and rederive PyPTO tile/buffer/scheduling settings for the target SoC rather than copying numeric examples.
